note: Unreached: JS-only shell. curl and WebFetch got only the title 'States - Material Design 3', no body text. Claim unverified, not disproven.

curl 403 twice, WebFetch loaded. SC 2.4.7 (AA): 'Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.' Covers focus only, not hover, pressed or disabled.

'0.1 second is about the limit for having the user feel that the system is reacting instantaneously, meaning that no special feedback is necessary'. Response time only; says no feedback is needed at 0.1 s, so it does not back drawing five states.
'Skeleton screens shorten the experience of waiting by enabling progressive loading'; the skeleton previews layout before data arrives. Design blog, not a study.
'Load content progressively as it becomes available' plus a progressiveLoad code sample. React tutorial page, not research.
'Subsecond load times would be ideal'; 'settling for being fast enough' is quoted. Page-speed targets only; nothing on shell or per-region loading.
'too many tabs reduces the tappable area of each tab and increases the complexity of your app'. Argues against many tabs; no side nav and no 5-section threshold.
'Avoid org-structure navigation... structure it according to the tasks and information your users most frequently need'. Task-based structure for header nav; no side-vs-top rule.
Notion sidebar with 'nested pages revealed by a disclosure triangle'. Design-blog teardown; supports nested sidebars, not the 5-section threshold or persistence.

curl 403 twice, WebFetch loaded. 'page structure should be consistent across different screen sizes' only 'If possible', and 'not a specific WCAG requirement'. No logo or search placement; nothing on page-to-page order.
'Utilize conventional top navigation or left navigation formats.' Supports conventional nav placement; not logo top-left, search top-right or a fixed order per page.
Redirected to www.shopify.com (same post). 'look and feel like they were designed by the same team'. Styling consistency across partner apps, not placement.
'your interface elements should complement the system's rhythm and tone, not clash with it'. Custom elements matching the system, not anchor placement.
'most users also expect to see a search function in the top right' and logo top-left. This is a news-story aside, not a finding of the 2006 Lindgaard study (the article is about first impressions).
'maintain that style across all your buttons so the user recognizes that they have a similar function'. Button-style consistency, not placement of logo, search or account.
Title says Booking kept the traditional breadcrumb after rejecting the two-dimensional one. Single A/B leak; no guideline, no two-level threshold, no current-nav.
Lists 'obstruction (artificially difficult processes)' as a dark pattern. Dark-pattern taxonomy; nothing on breadcrumbs, titles or current nav.
'effective in products ... organized in a hierarchy of more than two levels' and 'should never entirely replace the primary navigation'. Redirected to IBM's current guidelines page.
'should start with your home page and end with the parent section of the current page'. Ordering only; 'when to use' says 'multiple levels', with no two-level threshold.
curl 403 twice, WebFetch loaded. SC 2.4.2 (A) intent: 'the title of the page should also be changed dynamically to reflect the content or topic of the current view'.
'Use the active state to show users which page they have navigated to.'
'duplicated them as clickable actions just before the results'; the '0.5 Repeatability' figure matches. Sort options in a product list, not primary destinations.
'when the hamburger menu is closed, people don't know what's inside... we decided to go with a tab bar navigation system'. Apple's own usability finding.
'Menus shouldn't be hidden when you have plenty of space to display them.' Hamburger is 'a necessary evil on smaller screens'.
'poor search functionality contributed to the lower success rates' of Guardian and Huffington Post. Says 'due to'; page says 'contributed to'.
'average of 2.3 words per query' matches; users were 'confused' when results did not match every word. Query matching, not a visible scope or filter control.
Pattern 'Visible Search' tests a search bar against none. 'faster user navigation' is not on the page; test results are members-only.
'The search field is always visible in the header'; it 'keeps the search bar visible and accessible'.
'recent searches should be shown directly inline when the field becomes focused'; swipe to remove one, a header button clears all.
'The header can include a search bar.' Optional, not 'include'; the page also says some services omit search.
'Tested 8 times' matches. Text labels on three icon-only nav items gave 'a consistent increase in both menu clicks and sales'; 'clarity' not stated. Icon labels, not link vs button.
'use links when the desired action is to take the user to a new page'. Redirected to IBM's current guidelines page.
'Ensure that links and navigation systems are visually differentiated from normal text elements.' Covers the link-styling half only.

Tests a back link under checkout and a back button in the upper left. The claimed '+X.X%' is a masked placeholder on the page; 'reduce abandonment' is not stated. Back-link placement, not state restore.

'history.pushState()... matching the browser's back-button behavior'. The 90% is 'Of the e-commerce websites we benchmarked... over 90% get this wrong'; says widens it to all sites. Redirected to www.
'Always include a Back link component at the top of question pages to reassure them it's possible to go back and change previous answers.' Back half only; no URL per state.
'Back is supposed to lead back to the previous screen, essentially acting as an undo'. Previous screen, not up the hierarchy.
curl 403 twice, WebFetch loaded. SC 2.4.3 (A): 'focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability'. Focus-order half only; 2.1.1 reachability not cited.
Duplicate row: same page and same W3C org as the row above, so one organisation in the verdict count. Paraphrase matches the SC 2.4.3 text.
'Display form controls in the same order in the HTML as' on screen; 'Don't use CSS to rearrange the form controls.'
'Hide passwords by default until the user chooses to show it using the show button.' Password reveal; off-topic for focus order or shortcuts.
'Show shortcuts inline in results (⌘1, ⌘2), not hidden in tooltips'. One personal design guide about Raycast, not Raycast's own docs.
Recommended questions performed better below the results; the control had them 'higher above the results'. Second-hand leak.
'place your most important view so that it occupies or spans the upper-left corner of your dashboard'. The 'where users' eyes scan first' clause is not on the page.
'think about the most important thing someone needs to know at that moment'; hierarchy example: 'it's right at the top'.
'Primary metrics get the most prominent visual treatment'. Prominence, not top-left placement or order.
'limited to 4-7 chunks of information at any given moment with each chunk fades after 20-30 seconds'; 'ensure it's both necessary and relevant'.
Test removed dates, locations and product descriptions from list items. 'increase item density' is not on the page; outcome is members-only.
'Treatments that overwhelmed the visitor with information (FAQ, tabs) did not perform as well as hypothesized'. Landing-page test, not an app.
'grouping the categories into different logical sections, separated by a header title'. Grouping and dividers, not removing or hiding unused content.
'Show only what's relevant right now. Information should appear when needed and disappear when it's not.' Uber driver-facing principles, quoted by principles.design.
Memory-bias article; its filter example says users 'only view a small number of clothing items'. 'Limit visible items per screen to reduce cognitive load' is not stated.

why: No source is loads+says+backs yes: the M3 page is a JS-only shell (unverified), WCAG 2.4.7 covers focus only, and NN/g 0.1 s is response time.
onething.design and Steve Kinney back progressive, frame-first loading; the NN/g subsecond source is weak for per-region loading.
No source gives the 5-section side-nav threshold: Apple says limit tabs, USWDS says task-based header nav, Notion is a sidebar teardown.
Placement sources are tangential or hedged: NN/g says conventional top/left nav (weak), W3C is 'if possible' (partly), the Nature logo/search line is an aside, the rest are styling consistency.
IBM Carbon (breadcrumbs only past two levels), USWDS (active state marks current page) and W3C 2.4.2 (title changes per view) are all yes/yes/yes; GOV.UK and the Booking leak are weak.
Apple WWDC21 (hamburger hides features, tab bar instead) and NN/g (do not hide menus when there is room) are yes/yes/yes; the Bol leak is about sort options, weak.

Baymard (search always visible in header), MeasuringU (missing search cut completion) and Apple WWDC26 (recent searches inline on focus) are yes/yes/yes; scope or filter of results is thinly sourced (NN/g weak).
Carbon (use links for navigation) and Laws of UX (differentiate links visually) are yes/yes/yes; covers link-vs-button and link styling only; GoodUI icon labels is off-topic.

NN/g (Back goes to previous screen) and GOV.UK (Back link keeps answers changeable) are yes/yes/yes; the Smashing pushState source backs it but says partly (its 90% is e-commerce only); the URL-per-state half is thin.

USWDS (form order follows screen), W3C 2.4.3 (focus order preserves meaning; two rows, one org) and the Raycast guide (shortcuts inline) are yes/yes/yes; 2.1.1 reachability is not sourced and Raycast is one personal blog.

Tableau (most important view upper-left), Apple WWDC22 (purpose at top) and a GoodUI Google leak (primary results above recommended questions, second-hand) are yes/yes/yes; Odown is prominence, not position.

Laws of UX (4-7 chunks, necessary and relevant), MarketingSherpa/Intuit (overwhelming info with FAQs and tabs lost, landing-page test) and Uber (show only what is relevant now) are yes/yes/yes; the 55% work-area figure and hub-0002 are not in any source.
